stem: Which preventive vision-screening recommendation applies to an asymptomatic child who is 4 years old?

options.A: Screen vision at least once between ages 3 and 5 years to detect amblyopia or its risk factors
options.B: Routine screening should be deferred until adulthood if the child has no symptoms
options.C: A normal parental observation of the child's vision eliminates the need for screening
options.D: Screening at this age is intended to establish a definitive ophthalmologic diagnosis without referral

rationale: The USPSTF recommends vision screening at least once in children aged 3 to 5 years to detect amblyopia or its risk factors (Grade B). Screening identifies abnormalities requiring further assessment; it is not itself a definitive diagnosis.
educational_objective: Recognize the preventive vision-screening recommendation for children aged 3 to 5 years.
source_document_title: Vision in Children Ages 6 Months to 5 Years: Screening — Clinical Summary
source_locator: Clinical Summary, children aged 3 to 5 years
source_claim_supported: Supports screening at least once at ages 3–5 to detect amblyopia or its risk factors.
correction_summary: Reframed the original general rationale into the exact preventive-services recommendation and removed unsupported 'critical window' precision from the answer.
audit_findings: A exactly matches the recommendation. B-C improperly omit indicated screening; D confuses screening with diagnostic evaluation.
